subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — follow-up and sizing proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Amy Jones <amy.jones@shopwell.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — follow-up and sizing proposal

Hi Amy —

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to hear Shopwell's SLOs and production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate sizing on Dedicated: 

Recap / constraints you shared:
- Peak tail latency SLO: 95th <= 120ms for single-request text-gen (streaming allowed).
- Sustained throughput target: 400 tokens/sec during peak traffic windows (expected 9–11am PST).
- Concurrent sessions: up to 80 concurrent user sessions (each session issues streaming responses, avg 1.2 requests/sec).
- Max request length: 512 tokens, avg response length: 120 tokens.
- Streaming: client uses SSE, needs sub-200ms first-byte for streaming start.
- Data residency: US only (Dedicated in us-west).

Proposed validation plan / next steps:
1) Redwood to run targeted perf tests on two GPU configs (NVIDIA A100-40GB and H100-80GB) using Shopwell-like workload (attached sizing sheet).
2) We'll reserve a baseline reserved throughput bucket that matches ~500 tokens/sec to give headroom, and test burst handling to 800 tokens/sec.
3) Aditya / Dev will instrument KV cache hit/miss scenarios (prefix caching) and measure 95th latency with and without prefix cache.
4) We'll capture streaming first-byte times and provide a canary deployment plan to validate in your staging VPC.

I've attached a draft sizing workbook (shopwell_dedicated_sizing.xlsx) showing preliminary throughput/slot estimates and cost delta between A100 and H100. If that looks good, Aditya will schedule the perf run (we'll need a short window where Shopwell can route traffic or provide a replay trace).

Please confirm: is next-week Tue/Wed a good window for the perf run? Also, can your SRE share a ~10-minute representative replay or a small request trace (anonymized) that we can use to generate realistic arrival patterns?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Thanks Marissa — this lines up with our notes. A few clarifications: 

- The 120ms 95th target is strict for interactive product flows (search + explain). For background/batch flows we can accept higher latencies.
- Concurrency: 80 concurrent sessions is peak per region; global peak might be higher but we are only validating us-west for now.
- Streaming first-byte: we need <= 150ms for the first SSE event on average during normal load.

We can share a 10-minute anonymized replay — I'll coordinate with SRE and drop it in the Drive link you provided. Tue or Wed next week works; Tue morning PST would be ideal.

Also — regarding GPUs: are you expecting dramatically different latency profiles between A100 and H100 for our workload? Any rough ballpark on reserved throughput sizing (slots) so we can budget?

Thanks,
Amy
Head of Product
Shopwell
amy.jones@shopwell.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Amy Jones <amy.jones@shopwell.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — follow-up and sizing proposal

Amy — great, thanks. Short answers and what we'll deliver in the perf run:

1) A100 vs H100 expectation (ballpark):
- H100 tends to give ~15–30% lower 95th latency for transformer-decoder models at the same batch size because of TensorFloat and sparsity-friendly kernels; benefits are larger for very long sequences but still meaningful at 512 tokens.
- For streaming-first-byte (small initial generation), differences are smaller but H100 typically starts first-byte ~10–40ms faster under moderate load due to improved kernel startup and PCIe/CCIX differences.
- Cost delta: H100 reserved capacity is ~25–40% more expensive per-GPU-hour depending on region and commitment.

2) Reserved throughput sizing suggestion (initial baseline):
- Based on your targets (400 tokens/sec sustained, 80 concurrent sessions, avg 120 tokens per response), we recommend reserving capacity equivalent to 2 x A100-40GB slots (baseline) or 1 x H100-80GB + 1 x A100 as a mixed option for improved tail latency. This maps to ~500 tokens/sec baseline with room for autoscaling to 800 tokens/sec for short bursts.
- If Shopwell prefers stricter 95th under concurrent streaming, H100-heavy config is safer.

3) What we'll run in the perf test:
- Synthetic replay of your trace at 1x and 1.5x peak.
- KV/prefix cache scenarios: cold-start, warm cache (~70% hit), and degraded (~30% hit).
- Streaming latency measurements: first-byte and per-chunk intervals.
- Concurrency stress to confirm graceful degradation and fallback policies.

Aditya/Dev — can we schedule a 3-hour perf window on Tue 2027-06-22 09:00–12:00 PST? We'll need Shopwell to either point a staging VPC route or let us run against the replay file.

Amy — I'll update the sizing workbook with the A100/H100 delta and an estimated reserved-throughput SKU mapping. Expect that spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa

Looping in the infra team notes and plan: 

Marissa / Dev — we're good to run Tue 2027-06-22 09:00–12:00 PST. Plan: 
- Prep two test beds: (A) 2 x A100-40GB nodes with Redwood Dedicated reserved config; (B) 1 x H100-80GB + 1 x A100 for mixed config.
- We'll run the trace at 1x and 1.5x peak, capture 95th/99th latencies, first-byte streaming times, and token throughput.
- Instrument KV cache by replaying with injected prefixes to get ~70% hit and artificially drop to 30% for degraded tests.
- We'll collect per-request traces and upload a summarized report and the raw metrics to the Drive link.

Shopwell SRE — please share the anonymized replay by Mon EOD (2027-06-21) and confirm staging route or permission to run against the replay. Also share any request-level middleware (e.g., additional preprocessing) that could add ~20–30ms to first-byte so we can include it in measurements.

I'll attach the perf-run checklist to the Drive folder and the test artifact templates.
